questions.questionText: What best describes the problem of scarcity?

options.text: All consumer wants must be satisfied.
All resources are free at the point of use.
There are limited resources and unlimited wants.
There are unlimited resources and limited wants.

questions.questionText: What is an example of the purchase of a capital good?

options.text: a farm owner purchasing additional land
a farm owner purchasing a television
a farm owner purchasing a tractor
a farm worker purchasing some seeds

questions.questionText:
A student decides to buy a ticket for a concert instead of buying a new shirt.
What is the opportunity cost of buying the ticket?

options.text: the concert
the price of the ticket to the concert
the shirt
the time spent purchasing the ticket

questions.questionText: In a market system who has the most important role in influencing the allocation of resources?

options.text: consumers
entrepreneurs
government officials
producers

questions.questionText: What is an external cost of mining coal?

options.text: the cost of purchasing mining equipment
the extra cleaning costs of local residents’ houses because of coal dust
the extra cleaning costs of the mine buildings because of coal dust
the cost to the mine owners to remove waste

price quantity

What is the price elasticity of demand when the price falls from $0.50 to $0.45?

options.text: less than 0.5
between 0.5 and 1
between 1 and 1.5
greater than 1.5

questions.questionText: What is a function of a stock exchange?

options.text: It allows company shares to be traded.
It enables tourists to purchase foreign currency.
It provides a market for firms to sell their products.
It sets the rate of interest in an economy.

questions.questionText: What is a direct benefit to a worker of specialisation?

options.text: the higher output that may lead to higher earnings
the higher output that may lead to higher profits
the higher output that may lead to lower costs per unit produced
the longer training period that is required before starting work

questions.questionText:
A trade union succeeds in raising the wages in an industry above the equilibrium wage.
How would the demand and supply of labour change?
change in quantity change in quantity
of labour demanded of labour supplied

options.text: fall fall
fall rise
rise fall
rise rise

questions.questionText: What is most likely to result from an increase in income tax?

options.text: a fall in consumer spending
a fall in government spending
a rise in business investment
a rise in the level of imports

questions.questionText: Which statement explains why firms in perfect competition are not able to exploit consumers?

options.text: The firms can restrict output.
The products are differentiated.
There are barriers to entry.
There is perfect information.

questions.questionText:
A company with a chain of restaurants bought another chain of restaurants.
How is this purchase most likely to be classified?

options.text: conglomerate merger
diversification
horizontal integration
vertical integration

questions.questionText:
A company’s annual report suggested that it had benefited from some changes.
Which change is an internal economy of scale for this company?

options.text: an improvement in road and rail facilities that has reduced its distribution costs
an increase in the number of local specialist workers that it could recruit
the introduction of new training at a local college for which staff have enrolled
the reduction in the company’s costs by the purchase of a factory supplying components

questions.questionText:
A government believes that consumption of a certain good will be of benefit to society.
Which policy is most likely to encourage producers to increase their output of that good?

options.text: an increase in the period required for training the industry’s workers
an increase in the regulations affecting businesses
an increase in the subsidies for that good
an increase in the taxation of that good

questions.questionText: Which statement describes a progressive tax?

options.text: a tax that has a higher percentage rate as income rises
a tax that increases government income over time
a tax that places an increasing burden on the poor
a tax that rises in line with the rate of inflation

questions.questionText:
Which combination of government policies is most likely to reduce unemployment?
income government rate of
tax rate spending interest

options.text: decrease decrease increase
decrease increase decrease
increase decrease decrease
increase increase increase

questions.questionText: Which pair of government actions combines a fiscal policy with a supply-side policy?

options.text: changing government spending with changing interest rates
cutting tax rates with providing information on job vacancies
limiting bank lending with the privatisation of industry
restricting credit with less control over labour markets

questions.questionText: What is a recession?

options.text: a period when incomes rise by less than inflation
a period when prices are falling continuously for twelve months
a period when real GDP is declining for two consecutive quarters
a period when unemployment is rising

questions.questionText:
An economy is suffering from a period of deflation.
What does this mean for the economy?

options.text: Consumers may delay purchase of some products.
Purchasing power of consumers falls.
Tax revenues for the government will rise.
The real value of personal savings falls.

economic sectors.
economic change in

services +4
What could be concluded from this information?

options.text: Agricultural output fell.
The country became more developed.
The working population stayed constant.
Total employment remained the same.

questions.questionText:
Official statistics in 2010 showed South Africa had a very high unemployment rate at around
25%, although wages were double those in Brazil.
What might be a reason for South Africa’s high wages in a time of high unemployment compared
with Brazil?

options.text: a skilled workforce in Brazil
high levels of savings in South Africa
more labour-intensive production in Brazil
strong trade unions in South Africa

questions.questionText: What is a common feature of developed countries?

options.text: a high fertility rate
a low population
high net emigration
low birth rates

questions.questionText:
Which combination of changes in a government’s budget will lead to greater income inequality?
health and
direct taxes indirect taxes
education spending

options.text: decrease decrease increase
decrease increase decrease
increase decrease decrease
increase increase increase

questions.questionText:
The table shows the percentage of the working population in different sectors in three countries.
country agriculture (%) manufacturing (%) services (%)
Iran 38 33 29
Nepal 93 2 5
UK 2 42 56
What can be concluded from the table?

options.text: Iran has fewer people working in the secondary sector than the UK.
Nepal is a developed economy.
The tertiary sector is more developed in Iran than in Nepal.
The UK is dependent on the primary sector.

questions.questionText:
Which method of trade protection has the most predictable effect in controlling the level of
imports?

options.text: quotas on imports
safety and quality regulations for imports
subsidies to domestic producers
tariffs on imports

questions.questionText: What would cause a favourable change in the Indian trade in services (invisible) account?

options.text: A Japanese company invests in a subsidiary in India.
A large Indian company increases its exports of goods.
A Malaysian company increases its exports to India.
An Indian company wins a contract to transport South African exports.

questions.questionText:
In October 2015, one UK pound could be exchanged for 100 Indian rupees. By October 2016,
one UK pound could be exchanged for 80 Indian rupees.
What would be a short-term consequence of this change?

options.text: Economic growth in India would increase.
Indian manufacturers would earn higher profits from exports to the UK.
Inflationary pressure in the UK would reduce.
UK manufacturers would find it easier to export to India.

questions.questionText:
A country imports oil which is used in the production and distribution of goods. The country has
also experienced a rise in incomes which has resulted in a large increase in the demand for
goods, some of which it imports.
What is likely to happen to the country’s balance of trade in goods (visible) and to the price of oil?
balance of
price of oil
trade in goods
